newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Seat turnover 1.7 trln lire in '96.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Seat turnover 1.7 trln lire in '96.

text.p: Italian yellow pages publishing company Seat SpA, which is due to be privatised this year, posted sales of 1.73 trillion lire last year with an operating result of 497 billion lire, the company said in a statement.
It did not give comparative figures.
New orders for the year totalled 1.04 trillion lire by April 15, 75 percent of the whole year's budget target.
"Data from the first four months of the 1997 confirm the positive performance of Seat," the statement said.

Seat was split from state-controlled telecoms group Stet at the start of the year, with the Treasury taking over state industrial holding IRI's stake of around 61 percent. The Treasury has said due diligence on offers to buy the stake would be completed by mid-April and Seat sold by mid-June. In February, ITT Corp said it and other partners were seeking to acquire Seat. IRI is on record as saying it had received eight non-binding offers.

An Italian newspaper reported earlier this month that candidates in line to bid for the group had made much lower final offers than expected, adding that some of the candidates seemed to be having second thoughts. Italy's stock market council has estimated Seat's value at 2.34 trillion lire.
